questions.question: Identify the sentence that correctly uses inversion to emphasize the adverbial phrase.
options: Only after the rain had stopped did they begin the journey.
Only after the rain had stopped they began the journey.
Only after the rain had stopped began they the journey.
Only after the rain had stopped, they began the journey.
questions.answer: Only after the rain had stopped did they begin the journey.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly employs a cleft sentence to highlight the location?
options: It was in London that the meeting was held.
It was London where the meeting was held.
It was the meeting that was held in London.
London was where the meeting was held.
questions.answer: It was in London that the meeting was held.

questions.question: Select the option that correctly uses the subjunctive mood to express a hypothetical condition.
options: If I were you, I would accept the offer.
If I was you, I would accept the offer.
If I had been you, I would accept the offer.
If I had been you, I should accept the offer.
questions.answer: If I were you, I would accept the offer.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly demonstrates ellipsis, omitting the redundant part?
options: She doesn't like apples, whereas her brother does.
She doesn't like apples, whereas her brother does not.
She doesn't like apples, whereas her brother doesn't.
She doesn't like apples, whereas her brother likes not.
questions.answer: She doesn't like apples, whereas her brother does.

questions.question: Identify the sentence that appropriately uses a complex sentence structure with a non-restrictive relative clause to provide additional information.
options: The book, which was written by a famous author, sold well.
The book, that was written by a famous author, sold well.
The book was written by a famous author and sold well.
The book written by a famous author sold well.
questions.answer: The book, which was written by a famous author, sold well.
